subject: linear-algebra
subtopics: the matrix form Ax = b, the coefficient and augmented matrices, and the row and column pictures of a solution
the consistency test: rank(A) against rank([A|b]) and the three cases it produces
the square case: |A| not 0 gives a unique solution, |A| = 0 gives none or infinitely many
free variables, nullity n - rank(A), and the solution set as a particular solution plus the null space
homogeneous systems Ax = 0: always consistent, and a non-trivial solution exactly when rank(A) < n
solving by Gaussian elimination on [A|b] and back substitution
parameter-dependent systems: the critical values of the determinant and the consistency check at each
overdetermined and underdetermined systems: what m against n does and does not decide
the inverse and Cramer's rule, and the conditions under which they apply
the geometry of the three cases, including the triangular-prism arrangement of three planes
telling no solution apart from infinitely many solutions when the determinant vanishes

chosen.title: Linear Algebra (Gilbert Strang) Notes, Lecture 1 to 10
covers: the row picture, the column picture and the matrix form as three readings of Ax = b
the reachability condition: columns independent means every b is reachable, dependent columns means only some b are
forward elimination on the augmented matrix, the two ways elimination fails, and back substitution
the complete solution x = x_p + x_n, with free variables set to zero for the particular solution
chosen.why: The best readable English treatment of the column picture and of the particular-plus-null-space decomposition found this run, and it is written for GATE CSE readers on a GATE site rather than for a mathematics audience. Chosen over the NPTEL and IIT video sequences because their transcripts could not be retrieved at all, and over the coaching note sets because this one explains why the solution set has the shape it has instead of listing cases. Read in part: the fetched page covered the systems, elimination, multiplication, inverse and complete-solution sections; the later eigen and SVD sections were not needed here.

chosen.title: Matrices and Determinants - Consistency and Solution of Simultaneous Linear Equations (Lecture-04)
covers: the rank criterion r = s for consistency, and the unique and infinite sub-cases
the adjoint test when the coefficient determinant vanishes
the geometry of three planes keyed to the rank pair, including the triangular prism
the statement that a homogeneous system is always consistent
chosen.why: An IIT Kanpur initiative's own teaching text, and the only readable source found that gives the plane-arrangement table keyed to the rank pair, which the row-picture card needs. It also supplies the adjoint route into the singular case, which no other readable source gave in full. Read in part: the fetched page carried the linear-systems section and the eigen-value material that follows it; the later chapters were not needed.

chosen.title: Engineering Mathematics notes for GATE, Module 1, section 1.4 System of Linear Equations
covers: the consistency conditions stated as case 1 and case 2 with the split at r = number of unknowns
Cramer's rule and the inversion method X = A^(-1) B
the non-zero-solution condition for the homogeneous system as the vanishing of the coefficient determinant
chosen.why: A GATE coaching note set whose own contents page quotes the GATE CS linear algebra line word for word, so its scope matches the syllabus exactly, and it states Cramer's rule and the inversion method in the form GATE answers expect. Read in part: the direct PDF download failed from the sandbox again this run, so only the section 1.4 extract returned by the search service was read; the later chapters were not read at all.

chosen.channel: CareerCraft Labs (JEE mathematics notes in Hindi)
chosen.title: Notes on linear systems: raikhik samikaran nikay (Hindi)
covers: the three-case table in terms of the main determinant and the numerator determinants
the statement that a homogeneous system is never inconsistent, because the trivial solution is free
the warning that a zero main determinant alone does not mean infinitely many solutions
chosen.why: Chosen deliberately so that this topic is not built from English sources alone, and it is the only non-English source that was readable this run. It is a JEE-oriented chapter rather than a GATE lecture, so it is used only for the three points above, all of which are syllabus-neutral and stated more carefully here than in the English coaching notes. Every sentence taken from it is translated from Hindi into English and the card says so. Read in part: the fetched extract covered the determinants, the linear-systems table and the practice set; nothing past that was read.

chosen.channel: Ohio University, MATH3200 Applied Linear Algebra (Winfried Just)
chosen.title: Lecture 27: The Rank and Consistency of Systems of Linear Equations
covers: the theorem that Ax = b is consistent if and only if rank(A) = rank([A, b])
the corollary that rank(A) = m makes every system with that A consistent
worked inconsistent and consistent examples in echelon form
chosen.why: A university lecture that proves the consistency theorem rather than asserting it, and it is the only readable source that states the rank(A) = m corollary, which the overdetermined card needs for its one safe counting conclusion. Read in part: the PDF itself returned 502 from the sandbox, so only the text returned by the search service was read, which covered the theorem, the corollary and the two worked examples.

chosen.channel: GO Classes for GATE CS (Sachin Mittal)
chosen.title: Engineering Mathematics course, Linear Algebra lecture list: 3B-D on Ax = b, 4E-4F, 5D-5E, 6A-6C on rank and number of solutions
covers: the teaching order of the topic and the subtopic enumeration itself
confirmation that the GATE treatment runs from Ax = b through rank(A) against rank(A|b) to GATE PYQ work
chosen.why: Recorded because its lecture list is the closest fit to this syllabus line of any source found, and because it confirms the eleven subtopics are complete and in a sensible order: 3C writes the system as Ax = b with the geometric interpretation, 6B is solutions based on rank(A) and rank(A|b), 6C is questions on rank and the number of solutions. No card quotes it and no claim rests on it, because no transcript could be retrieved this run.

standard_refs: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra (the column picture, elimination, the complete solution x = x_p + x_n)
Lay, Linear Algebra and Its Applications (the consistency theorem and the rank conditions)
Hoffman and Kunze, Linear Algebra (solutions of homogeneous and non-homogeneous systems)
Kolman and Hill, Elementary Linear Algebra with Applications (Cramer's rule and the geometry of the three cases)
note: Every rank, determinant, solution and parameter value published in this topic is recomputed by check_system_of_linear_equations() in scripts/validate.py, by Gaussian elimination over the rationals, including exhaustive small-integer enumeration for the rank criteria, the nullity count, the non-trivial-solution test, the two-solutions-imply-infinitely-many claim and every counterexample quoted on a card. No source is quoted; each card paraphrases and then re-derives. The one non-English source is Hindi, read in part, and every sentence taken from it is translated and marked as translated on the cards that use it. No video transcript could be retrieved this run, so the GATE-oriented lecture sequence is recorded as structure only.
